newsitem.title: JAPAN: SWIMMING-RILEY SETS UP SHOWDOWN WITH RIVAL HEYNS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-RILEY SETS UP SHOWDOWN WITH RIVAL HEYNS.

text.p: Australia's Samantha Riley set up a showdown with South African rival and double Olympic champion Penny Heyns in the 200 metres breaststroke at the Pan Pacific Swimming Championships on Wednesday.
Overall, Americans qualified first in five of the eight preliminary events on the last day of the meeting and are also heavily favoured in the two medley relays to be run on Wednesday evening.
Riley topped all qualifiers in the women's 200 breaststroke in two minutes 27.97 seconds, while Heyns, who won the event and the 100 breaststroke at Atlanta, was second in 2:28.56.

Riley has already knocked off Heyns in the 100 in Fukuoka, a win which she said helped ease some of the pain caused by the accusations made against her after testing positive in a doping test in late 1995 after she took a headache pill.
Although she was eventually cleared, Riley did not recover her top form in time for the Olympics and finished third in the 100.
The most surprising result for the Americans came from 31-year-old Ron Karnaugh, who qualified first in the men's 200 individual medley.
"It's amazing," said Karnaugh's coach, Dick Shoulberg.
"He just loves to swim and is a great role model."
Karnaugh, who graduated from medical school in May, first made the U.S. national team in 1986.
He placed sixth in the 200 individual medley at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics six days after his father died during the opening ceremonies.
Fellow American Kristine Quance topped the heats in the women's 200 individual medley after winning the 400 individual medley on Monday.

Americans finished one-two in both the men's 50 freestyle and men's 200 breaststroke, with Tom Wilkens finishing ahead of Kurt Grote in the 200, and William Pilczuk edging out David Fox in the 50 freestyle.

And Brooke Bennett, the Olympic gold medalist in the women's 800 freestyle, will be trying to fight off Costa Rica's Claudia Poll in the 800 final. Poll has already won the women's 200 and 400 freestyle races in the quickest times of the year.
World-record holder Le Jingyi gave China its best shot at a gold in Fukuoka by qualifying first in the women's 50 freestyle.
American Jenny Thompson, who beat Le Jingyi to the gold in the 100 freestyle, qualified second.
Australia's 17-year-old Grant Hackett, after winning the 400 freestyle in the ninth-fastest time ever, will be looking to go under 15 minutes in the men's 1,500 freestyle final.
About 300 swimmers from 22 countries and regions are competing in the Pan Pacific Championships.
